input.command: grep -rn "runnable\|createFixTask\|poll\|TaskStore" src | grep -v "^src/tasks.ts"; ls; ls test* tests 2>/dev/null

input.reason:
In src/tasks.ts, createFixTask (lines 13-19) builds a local `task` with `state: "running", feedback: null` and inserts it (line 15). It then writes the feedback with a separate `store.update(id, { feedback })` (line 16). That update never changes the local object. So `emit({ ...task })` on line 17 and `return task` on line 18 always carry `feedback: null`, even though the store now holds the real feedback. This stale emit happens on every call and does not depend on timing.

The race part also follows from the code. The task is stored as already "running" and without feedback, and the insert and the update are two separate awaited writes. A concurrent `poll` (lines 21-25) that calls `store.runnable()` between them can get the task with null feedback and pass it to `run`. The repo has no TaskStore implementation that would make the two writes atomic or keep `runnable()` from returning this row. Whether `runnable()` includes "running" tasks cannot be checked, because no store implementation is in the tree. The stale emit alone confirms the defect.
input.failure_scenario: A caller runs createFixTask(store, "t1", "please fix lint", emit). The store row gets feedback "please fix lint", but emit gets { id: "t1", state: "running", feedback: null }, and the function also returns null feedback. Any listener, such as a dashboard update, shows or acts on a task with no feedback. Separately, if poll runs between the insert on line 15 and the update on line 16, it can pass the already-"running", feedback-less task to run(), so the fix runs without its instructions.
input.severity_reason: The stale feedback in the emitted and returned task is certain and happens on every createFixTask call, so this is wrong behavior on the main path. The race makes it worse: a task can run with no feedback. There is no data corruption in the store and no security impact, so it is not Critical.
